comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Most of this went away with d808ec1. A pane the daemon denies is now taken off screen the moment it refuses a focus or a close, so the specific dead square in the report - a phantom pane - can be dismissed by trying to dismiss it.

What is left is narrower: a bridge that fails for some other reason (no herdr, a socket that went) still leaves Ghostty's own `Press any key to close the window` screen, and no key reaches it. Keystrokes in a pane go to the core and out to that pane's channel; nothing is ever sent to the surface, so the surface never sees the key it is asking for.

The hook for this exists and we decline it: libghostty's `close_surface_cb` fires with whether the process is still alive, and `Renderer.swift` answers nothing. Wiring it would let the shell know a pane's command exited, mark that pane not typeable, and say so on the chrome - which is both a better screen than Ghostty's and one keystroke fewer that goes nowhere.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
When a bridge cannot attach, the surface shows Ghostty's own `failed to launch the requested command` screen, ending in `Press any key to close the window.` No key does. Clicking it does not move the keyboard there either, so the pane cannot be focused, cannot be closed, and cannot be dismissed - it just sits there taking half the window.

Two reasons, both ours. Keystrokes in a pane go to the core and out to that pane's channel; nothing is ever sent to the libghostty surface itself, so the surface never sees the key it is asking for. And a click asks the core to focus that pane, which refuses when the daemon does not hold it - so the request that would move the keyboard is exactly the one that fails.

What a person needs here is a way out that does not depend on the pane being alive: closing it should work on Muster's side even when the daemon refuses, since a pane the daemon denies is one that is not coming back.

Found alongside the phantom-pane card, and worth fixing separately - a failed bridge for any reason lands here.

Reported from a real window, 2026-08-15.
title: 🧯 A pane whose bridge failed is a dead square you cannot dismiss
